style.observation: Forest-green/ochre controlled relief-print grammar with flat ink mass, directional hatch, crisp plate boundaries and interlocking curved shade/light/page shapes.

substantive_visual.observation: Full lamp structure, light under shade, stacked books and broad open-book/page planes substantively express a desk-light experience and organize the image.

excluded_template.observation: Curved shade crosses above/into title zone; light plane expands diagonally into reading area and page contours connect across lower image. Image construction actively shapes the layout rather than serving as a small adjunct to passive headline/information fields.

product_identity.observation: Entire supplied product identity remains once: wide horizontally curved forest-green shade, paired connected supports and shared low oval base. Product photograph background/coordinates were not preserved because not requested.

hangul.observation: Main descriptions have consistent mature serif syllable proportions, visible open counters, moderate stroke contrast and readable word gaps. Smaller visit column is coherent but has less scale than main paragraphs.

information_relationship.observation: Actual route is full lamp/long shade to title and English product line, then two adjacent descriptions, event below, schedule/place and adjacent visit/invitation/URL. No essential sentence is split among corners.

function_contact.observation: Both supports visibly join shade and shared base; base rests stably in desk/book-plane setting. No hands/people requested.

material_edges.observation: Directional hatch respects curved shade/page planes, plate boundaries and page strata remain precise. No visibly broken support or accidental product crop.

selection_reason.comparison: Initial preserves a wider lamp base but compresses all descriptions/visit copy into tiny single lines. Repair-1 enlarges some copy but leaves description sizes uneven and headline scale unchanged. Repair-2 most improves ordinary-use paragraph reading and invitation grouping while retaining complete product, required print grammar and copy. Selection is based on viewed outcomes, not recency.
